<reflection>
The first experiment provided a baseline dataset where many mechanisms fit similarly well, with M7 having the best fit (NLL ≈ -23.82) and M20 being a clear outlier (NLL ≈ -10.83). The small differences among the other mechanisms (NLL range -23.8 to -22.3) indicate that the data from a single moderate condition is insufficient to discriminate them. The aim of obtaining a broad baseline was achieved, but we now need to design an experiment that will spread out the NLL differences across mechanisms by probing their distinct kinetic predictions.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Reducing the catalyst concentration by an order of magnitude (from 0.02 M to 0.002 M) while keeping substrate constant (2.0 M) and no initial product will test the dependence of the reaction rate on catalyst concentration. Mechanisms with linear catalyst dependence (e.g., simple Michaelis-Menten M1) will predict a proportional decrease in initial rate, while those with dimerization (M2, M3) or bimolecular catalyst steps (M5, M19) will show a more pronounced decrease (quadratic or higher order). Deactivation mechanisms (M9–M20) may exhibit different relative deactivation extents at lower catalyst, affecting the time course shape. This condition avoids saturation or depletion extremes and should yield a slower, well-resolved time course that, when combined with the first run, will help discriminate a wide range of mechanisms through their scaling behavior.
</hypothesis>
